name: Stryker
description: Stryker makes medical technology sold to hospitals and surgeons in about 61 countries: joint-replacement and trauma implants with the Mako surgical robot (Orthopaedics, 38 percent of 2025 sales), and everything else used in an operating room or ambulance (MedSurg and Neurotechnology, 62 percent): surgical instruments, endoscopy cameras, hospital beds and emergency equipment, neurovascular and stroke devices. Revenue comes from implants and disposables used per procedure plus capital equipment (robots, cameras, beds), and capital sales are generally higher in the fourth quarter. Growth has been bought as well as organic: it acquired Inari Medical (venous clot removal) in 2025 for $4.8B net of cash and sold its Spinal Implants business in 2025, which is why Orthopaedics grew only 4 percent in 2025 while the company grew 11 percent.

sub.name: Surgical and hospital devices and diagnostics

gics.note: SEC SIC code 3841 (Surgical and Medical Instruments and Apparatus). About 38% of sales is orthopedic implants and the rest is a wide range of hospital equipment and disposables.

hq.note: 1941 Stryker Way, Portage, MI 49002 (SEC EDGAR business address). Wikipedia's S&P 500 table lists Kalamazoo, Michigan.

employees.note: Approximately 56,000 employees globally, about 28,000 in the US; FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: MedSurg and Neurotechnology
businessLines.shareBasis: Share of revenue per 10-K (62%). Share of profit = 4,672 / 7,492 total segment operating income.
businessLines.how: Customers buy capital equipment (the 10-K lists surgical equipment, navigation, endoscopic and communications systems, patient handling and emergency medical equipment), which the 10-K says sells more in Q4, plus repeat disposables and instruments; Inari and neurovascular products are single-use devices bought per procedure.
businessLines.description: Instruments (surgical equipment; Steri-Shield operating-room protection systems), Endoscopy (visualization and communications systems), Medical (patient handling, emergency medical equipment, intensive-care and incontinence products), Vascular (Neurovascular plus Inari's venous thromboembolism products), Neuro Cranial.

revenue.note: FY2024 $13,518M; FY2023 $12,163M. Q2 2026 about $3,625M and H1 2026 about $6,832M (computed as total net sales minus Orthopaedics)

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $13,518M; FY2023 $12,163M. Q2 2026 about $3,625M and H1 2026 about $6,832M (computed as total net sales minus Orthopaedics)

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating income before corporate costs ($889M), amortization ($732M) and acquisition charges; FY2024 $4,004M

businessLines.name: Orthopaedics
businessLines.how: Hospitals buy implants for each joint replacement or trauma case, and the Mako robotic-arm technology is used in knee and hip procedures (the 10-K reports Mako procedure counts, not how the robot itself is priced or placed).
businessLines.description: Implants for hip and knee joint replacement and for trauma and extremity surgery, sold with the Mako SmartRobotics platform (available in more than 45 countries; over one million robotic Mako Total Knee procedures done to date).

brands.name: Mako SmartRobotics
brands.share: More than 2 million robotic procedures across Total Knee, Total Hip and Partial Knee to date; over 1 million Total Knee; in more than 45 countries (FY2025 10-K)

brands.name: Inari Medical
brands.share: Acquired 2025 at $80 per share, $4,810M net of cash acquired; Vascular sales $1,968M FY2025 combined with Neurovascular
